name: Rituals for Dying Into Other Worlds
description:
Image Credits: Lagori Collective
Death is the moment where the question of plural worlds becomes most personal. Every culture has answered it differently. Some say you move to another world, some say you dissolve back into this one and some say you join a world of ancestors running alongside the living. There are lots of different understandings of what the world is, who inhabits it, and what it means to leave it.

Most of us have inherited rituals for death without choosing them. And most of those rituals were designed only for humans. This workshop asks: what if we designed them ourselves for every world, every species, every relationship that ends? 

Using a ritual design framework created by Lagori Collective, participants will be invited to sit with death as a transition between worlds and to begin designing the ritual that would mark that crossing on their own terms.

This event is part of Plural Worlds, developed in collaboration with Lagori Collective and presented in conjunction with Beneath the Turning Sky.

name: How Do We Know The Universe?
description:
A moderated conversation exploring knowledge systems that often remain outside textbooks, including community ecologies, urban land reading, and cultural practice. Moving through three questions—what it means to know the world from where one stands and whose standing has historically counted; what knowledge about the natural world exists in the city that dominant frameworks cannot see; and what might change in how the future is imagined if these other ways of knowing were taken seriously—the session invites audiences to briefly inhabit a world other than the one they walked in with.

This event is part of Plural Worlds, developed in collaboration with Lagori Collective and presented in conjunction with Beneath the Turning Sky.

name: Counter Mapping: Local Realities
description:
We all carry maps of the places we know: the street we take home, the room we grew up in, the neighbourhoods we navigate every day. But what do these maps leave out? What might happen if we mapped not only buildings and roads, but also water, heat, birds, memories, labour, decay, waiting, migration, infrastructure, and imagined futures? What if a familiar place could be encountered as one that holds several worlds at once?
Facilitated by Ishita Jain from Living Midnight Narrative Outfit, participants will choose a familiar and intimate place and begin to map its invisible territories. Through drawing, tracing, layering, and juxtaposition, they will explore its environmental, biological, social, infrastructural, and temporal layers, while considering the futures that might already be latent within these relationships.
As the maps take shape, they may begin to move beyond conventional representations of place, becoming fields of movement, encounters, and possibilities. The aim is not to create a more accurate map of a familiar world, but to explore what becomes visible when the way of seeing it changes.

This event is part of Plural Worlds, developed in collaboration with Lagori Collective and presented in conjunction with Beneath the Turning Sky.

name: Futures Walk
description:
Image Credits: Vidit Jain
This walk invites participants to move slowly, attending closely to the many worlds that coexist within the same stretch of the city: ecological, historical, multispecies, and everyday. Walking then becomes a way of sensing these plural worlds and the futures already being rehearsed within them.

Simple prompts will guide attention along the way: What exists here that no map would show? Whose world is this, and whose has it been? What futures are already present in this neighbourhood, waiting to be noticed?

The walk begins at MAP and moves through Cubbon Park before concluding at the Central State Library. Along the route, participants will sense and gather local, place-based imaginations of the future, considering urban ecologies, recreation, local economies, and community.

The session will close with a collective reflection, inviting participants to ask: What worlds did we walk through, and which ones were invisible to us before today?

This event is part of Plural Worlds, developed in collaboration with Lagori Collective and presented in conjunction with Beneath the Turning Sky.
